2a(1).fact: Brake fluid is hygroscopic and readily absorbs water vapor from outside air, which lowers its boiling point and causes brake fade under heavy use.
2a(1).misconception: Opening the brake fluid reservoir cap frequently is a harmless habit for visual fluid checks.
2a(1).pamphlet_summary: Inspect the translucent master cylinder reservoir to verify that fluid rests between the minimum and maximum indicator lines without removing the cap unnecessarily. Check for dark amber or black discoloration that indicates contamination or moisture absorption requiring a system flush (p. 25).
2a(1).socratic_question: Why is the brake fluid reservoir made of see-through plastic rather than solid metal?

2a(2).fact: Detergent additives intentionally suspend microscopic soot and combustion byproducts in the oil to keep internal engine passages clean between scheduled oil changes.
2a(2).misconception: Engine oil turns black exclusively because the engine has suffered internal mechanical damage.
2a(2).pamphlet_summary: Park the vehicle on level ground and withdraw the dipstick, wiping it clean before reinserting it fully to obtain an accurate reading. Confirm that the oil level registers between the add and full hash marks while observing the oil clarity and viscosity (p. 21).
2a(2).socratic_question: What does wiping the dipstick with a clean rag before taking a reading prevent?

2a(3).fact: Engines require a balanced mixture of distilled water and ethylene glycol coolant to inhibit internal corrosion and prevent both boiling over in summer and freezing solid in winter.
2a(3).misconception: Adding pure tap water to a low cooling system provides the exact same protection as premixed antifreeze.
2a(3).pamphlet_summary: Observe the coolant level through the transparent overflow recovery tank to ensure it aligns with the cold fill mark while the engine remains unheated. Never loosen or remove a pressurized radiator cap on a hot cooling system due to the extreme risk of scalding steam eruption (p. 29).
2a(3).socratic_question: How does an expansion tank allow you to check engine coolant safely without exposing yourself to pressurized boiling liquid?

2a(4).fact: Many modern passenger vehicles use fully electric power steering systems that operate with an electric motor instead of hydraulic fluid.
2a(4).misconception: Every modern passenger car contains a hydraulic power steering reservoir that drivers must check regularly.
2a(4).pamphlet_summary: Locate the hydraulic power steering reservoir and read the hot or cold level indicators on the built-in cap dipstick. Modern vehicles with electric power steering assist lack hydraulic pumps and reservoirs entirely, requiring no fluid inspection (p. 31).
2a(4).socratic_question: Why do some vehicles have both hot and cold measurement marks on the power steering dipstick?

2a(5).fact: Dish soap leaves a gummy film that clogs fine washer spray nozzles and strips protective wax coatings off vehicle paint.
2a(5).misconception: Ordinary tap water mixed with dish soap works as an effective substitute for commercial windshield washer fluid.
2a(5).pamphlet_summary: Identify the windshield washer reservoir by the windshield spray icon stamped on its cap and top off the reservoir with seasonal washer solvent. Plain water should never replace commercial washer fluid because water freezes inside the lines and lacks glass cleaners (p. 19).
2a(5).socratic_question: What could happen to the washer reservoir and pump if plain water is left in the tank during subfreezing winter temperatures?

2a(6).fact: Most automatic transmissions require the engine to idle in park so the internal hydraulic pump fills the torque converter and valve passages during dipstick measurement.
2a(6).misconception: Automatic transmission fluid must always be inspected with the engine completely shut off just like engine oil.
2a(6).pamphlet_summary: Check automatic transmission fluid on a level surface with the engine running at idle and the transmission in park after the fluid reaches operating temperature. Pull the brightly colored transmission dipstick to confirm proper fluid level and inspect the fluid for a healthy translucent red color free of burnt odors (p. 23).
2a(6).socratic_question: What does a dark brown color accompanied by an acrid burnt smell indicate when examining transmission fluid on a paper towel?

2a(7).fact: Only pure distilled water should be added to low battery cells because minerals in tap water contaminate the plates and the sulfuric acid itself does not evaporate.
2a(7).misconception: Low battery electrolyte in an unsealed battery cell should be refilled with sulfuric battery acid or municipal tap water.
2a(7).pamphlet_summary: Examine unsealed battery vent caps to confirm electrolyte covers the lead plates, adding only distilled water if plates are exposed. Inspect terminals for white or blue powdery corrosion, cleaning dirty posts with a wire brush and a neutralized baking soda solution while wearing eye protection (p. 34).
2a(7).socratic_question: How can powdery terminal corrosion prevent a vehicle from starting even when the battery holds a full internal charge?

8a(1).fact: The alternator generates all electrical current for the vehicle once the engine runs, while also replenishing energy that the starter motor drew from the battery.
8a(1).misconception: A vehicle battery continuously supplies all electrical power to the spark plugs, lights, and electronics while driving down the highway.
8a(1).pamphlet_summary: Test the battery, starter motor, alternator, and drive belt to verify that the charging system produces roughly 13.5 to 14.5 volts while the engine runs. Inspect the starter solenoid wiring and verify that the alternator belt retains proper tension without glazing or cracking (p. 59).
8a(1).socratic_question: If the dashboard battery warning light illuminates while driving, which component has likely stopped functioning?

8a(2).fact: The propulsion inverter in a hybrid or electric vehicle manages hundreds of volts by converting direct current from the high-voltage battery into alternating current to spin the electric traction motors.
8a(2).misconception: An automotive inverter functions only as an interior power outlet adapter to run standard household appliances from the cigarette lighter.
8a(2).pamphlet_summary: Identify the electric drive inverter by its dedicated cooling lines and high-voltage orange insulated cabling, understanding that it transforms direct current from the traction pack into multiphase alternating current. Never touch or probe orange high-voltage cables or inverter terminals because traction batteries carry lethal electrical potential (p. 65).
8a(2).socratic_question: Why are all high-voltage cables and connections in hybrid and electric vehicles color-coded bright orange?

8a(3).fact: Skin oils deposited onto quartz halogen glass create concentrated hot spots that cause the bulb envelope to blister and burn out prematurely.
8a(3).misconception: Touching the glass bulb of a halogen headlight with bare fingers during installation causes no physical harm to the lamp.
8a(3).pamphlet_summary: Conduct a complete walkaround inspection checking headlights, taillights, brake lights, turn signals, and hazard flashers for proper illumination and clean lenses. When replacing halogen headlight bulbs, hold the replacement unit strictly by its base to prevent natural skin oils from overheating and shattering the quartz glass capsule (p. 63).
8a(3).socratic_question: Why is having an assistant press the brake pedal necessary when performing a complete lighting check on a vehicle?
